title: An example leaves the trap centre where it was, so after the centre has been moved the examples no longer look like their names, and the list still names them
repro: python tools/shot.py --url dist/v8.html --actions out/t9/solids/ex.json (steps 20 to 22). By hand on dist/v8.html, helpers as in solids-1 of the first check: type('col-txNum','0.5'); type('col-tyNum','0.3'); sel('trapExamples',4); then sel('trapExamples',1); then sel('trapExamples',8);
expected: The named object, as in out/t9/solids/ex-4.png, ex-1.png and ex-8.png. Either an example puts the trap centre back to 0, 0, 0, or the hint names the trap centre among the things that give a different object and the list does not show the example's name while the centre is elsewhere.
actual: Chain of bubbles gives lopsided bubbles with torn patches, Spiky coral gives a few scattered sprigs, Rings in the lace gives a turquoise sheet that fills the lower part of the picture and runs out of the frame. The trap centre stays at (0.5, 0.3, 0); the list reads 'Chain of bubbles', 'Spiky coral', 'Rings in the lace' and exampleAt() returns 3, 0, 7. The hint lists what an example sets and says 'Everything else stays as you left it, so with another approach, power or equation the same example gives a different object': the trap centre is not mentioned. Judged at 0.21 of full size.
evidence: out/t9/solids/ex3-4-centre.png, ex3-1-centre.png, ex3-8-centre.png against ex-4.png, ex-1.png, ex-8.png; sheet-ex.png (third row); ex.log steps 20 to 22
suggested_fix: src/js/75-presets.js: add tx, ty, tz to EXAMPLE_KEYS with 0 in each EXAMPLES entry, so applyExample() puts the centre back and exampleFits() stops naming an example while the centre is elsewhere. Add 'and centre' to the hint (trapExamplesHelp, built in boot()).

title: With 'Orbit steps the trap reads' above 4, a further step repaints whole areas once zoomed in, where the help promises a finer pattern on top
repro: python tools/shot.py --url dist/v8.html --actions out/t9/solids/reach.json (steps 8 to 12 Mandelbrot, 20 to 24 Julia). By hand: $('mode-j').click(); type('cxNum','-1'); type('cyNum','0'); type('czNum','0'); type('col-radiusNum','0.7'); double-click the middle of the solid and zoom in until the distance to it is an eighth (the script sets L.cam.target to L.pick() at the middle of the stage and L.cam.dist to an eighth of the distance); then type('col-reachNum','4'); type('col-reachNum','6'); type('col-reachNum','16');
expected: The help under the dial: 'A low number gives broad, calm areas of colour. Each further step draws a finer pattern on top.' So the broad areas keep their colour and gain detail.
actual: Zoomed in 8 times the whole face changes hue with the dial. Julia c = -1, shell 0.7: turquoise at 4, green at 6 to 16; 94.5 % of the pixels differ between 4 and 6. Opening Mandelbrot: violet at 2, blue at 6, turquoise at 9 and 16; 41.0 %, 49.3 % and 73.0 % differ between 2 and 4, 4 and 6, 6 and 9. At the opening view the same moves change 0.5 to 2.9 % of the pixels and nothing above 6. So with the dial raised, the colours of whole areas change as the user zooms in; at the starting value 4 they hold (rabbit, zoom 8: at most 0.8 % of pixels moved). The help does not say that 4 is the value that keeps colours in place.
evidence: out/t9/solids/sheet-rc.png (rc-m-z8-2.png, -4, -6, -9, -16; rc-b-z8-4.png, rc-b-z8-16.png); numbers printed at the end of the dial run, repeated in the checks
suggested_fix: src/js/25-colour.js, COLOUR_CONTROLS key 'reach', help: say that a higher number also changes the colour of whole areas once you zoom in, and that 4 keeps the colours in place while zooming. Or, in colourReach() (GL_COLOUR), let a step that comes in with the zoom fade in on top of the colour already there.

title: Kleinian trap solid: moving the trap centre along y gives a black or filled picture, and no note says why
repro: On dist/v8.html: const $ = id => document.getElementById(id); $('mode-k').click(); document.querySelectorAll('details.sec').forEach(d => { d.open = true; }); const t = $('col-solid'); t.value = [...t.options].find(o => o.text === 'Is the solid').value; t.dispatchEvent(new Event('change', { bubbles: true })); const e = $('col-tyNum'); e.focus(); e.value = '0.5'; e.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true })); e.dispatchEvent(new KeyboardEvent('keydown', { key: 'Enter', bubbles: true })); Then the same with 0.25 and 1. Step file out/t9/kleinian/n1.json, steps 6 to 9.

title: The sentence about the Drawing radius goes away when the user zooms out, which is when the solid is drawn cut off
repro: On dist/v8.html: const L = squaringLab, $ = id => document.getElementById(id); $('mode-k').click(); const e = $('kinvrNum'); e.focus(); e.value = '3'; e.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true })); e.dispatchEvent(new KeyboardEvent('keydown', { key: 'Enter', bubbles: true })); Read #kleinWarn (both sentences show). title: A trap solid's small hollow shows something different in a larger or finer file than on the screen
repro: PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 python out/t9/export/colours.py S s1 t1 k1 s2 t2   then look at the tiles around stage pixel (490, 440). By hand on dist/v8.html at 1400 x 950: document.getElementById('mode-j').click(); const e = document.getElementById('col-solid'); e.value = [...e.options].find(o => o.text.startsWith('Is the solid')).value; e.dispatchEvent(new Event('change', { bubbles: true })); wait until drawn and look at the hollow a little right of the middle and below it (57% across, 63% down). Then Save a picture: Size 'Twice the size on screen' or '3840 x 2160 (4K)', Quality 'As on screen now', PNG, Start, Save the file, and compare the hollow.
expected: With Quality 'As on screen now' the file shows what the screen shows at every size, as it does for the Mandelbrot, Julia, Kleinian and 2D pictures (hue 99th percentile under 5 degrees) and as the panel's first sentence promises ('It is the picture as it is when you press Start').
actual: Screen at Balanced, and the file at the same size and quality (worst difference 1): a hollow about 60 pixels wide holding a red ragged lump with a torn dark rim. Twice the size, same quality: the hollow is almost closed into a smooth dish with a faint ring. 4K, same quality: a smooth dish with a small rainbow ball. Screen size at Fine and Extra fine: a larger red ball; twice at Fine: closed, with a red speck. The rest of the solid agrees (hue median 0.0 to 0.6 degrees); the hollow alone gives 0.5 to 0.7% of coloured pixels more than 45 degrees off at twice and 4K, against 0.00% for the other pictures at the same quality. Only this one trap solid was tried; solids with many thin layers may change more. It looks like the screen's side of solids-5 (thin layers removed in patches where the wall is under two pixels): a larger file has more pixels across the same wall, so the layer stays. That cause is reasoned from ROUND9, not checked in the code.

If the engineer working on solids-5 makes a layer go or stay as a whole, re-run the reproduction: it may cure this too.

title: The model of the example "Sea urchins" is covered in fins that the picture does not show
repro: Open dist/v8.html. In Colour and light choose "Sea urchins" in the list Examples (console: const e = document.getElementById('trapExamples'); e.value = [...e.options].find(o => o.text.startsWith('Sea urchins')).value; e.dispatchEvent(new Event('change', { bubbles: true }));). Wait for the picture, open Save a 3D model, press Start the model (128 cells, offset 0.5), save, open julia-128.ply or .stl. From the workspace root: PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 python out/t9/mesh/drive.py x exurchins:128,256 exurchins0:128 then python out/t9/mesh/check.py exurchins-128 exurchins-256 exurchins0-128 and look at out/t9/mesh/pics/cmp-exurchins-128.png (left the page, middle the model from the same camera, right the outlines, blue is model only).
expected: A model of what the picture shows: smooth balls with a few dozen clear spikes.
actual: At 128 cells the balls are covered all over with small fins and flakes: 26% of the outline is model only, overlap 0.78 (the other standard models reach 0.95 to 0.97), 'The largest of 1,729' pieces. At 256 cells still 14.5% and overlap 0.853, 7,962 pieces. With Surface offset 0 the same solid at 128 gives the picture's shape: overlap 0.902, 4% model only, 35 pieces, no warning. So the half-cell offset, together with the rule that keeps parts thinner than a cell, grows hair-thin spikes that the picture never draws into fins. The panel's warning says 'A higher resolution follows the picture more closely', which helps little here; it does not mention the offset, which does help.
evidence: out/t9/mesh/pics/cmp-exurchins-128.png ; same folder: cmp-exurchins-256.png, sheet-offset0.png (second row: offset 0) ; numbers in out/t9/mesh/check-edge.txt and check-d.txt ; panel text in out/t9/mesh/runs/exurchins-128.json
suggested_fix: src/js/46-mesh.js, meshTrue() and meshPit(): a 'pit' sample keeps its plain, short estimate so that parts thinner than a cell survive, and the level of half a cell then thickens every such hair. Keep that margin only for parts the picture also shows (for example only where the part is connected over several cells, or not for a trap that is the solid), or drop pieces and fins smaller than about a cell before the offset is applied. Failing that, when many pieces appear at an offset above 0, let #meshWarn say that a smaller surface offset follows the picture more closely.

title: Models of the Julia examples carry other colours than the picture: "Chain of bubbles" is teal instead of a rainbow swirl, "Sea urchins" is confetti instead of green
repro: Open dist/v8.html, choose "Chain of bubbles" in the list Examples (#trapExamples), wait for the picture, Start the model at 128 cells, save, open julia-128.ply with its vertex colours. From the workspace root: PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 python out/t9/mesh/drive.py x exbubbles:128,256 exurchins:128,256 exarches:128,256 then python out/t9/mesh/check.py exbubbles-128 exbubbles-256 exurchins-128 exurchins-256 exarches-128 exarches-256; pictures out/t9/mesh/pics/cmp-ex*.png, sheet out/t9/mesh/pics/sheet-cmp-ex.png.
expected: The model carries the picture's colours, as it now does for the ordinary solids (median hue difference 2 to 8 degrees).
actual: Chain of bubbles at 128 cells: the picture is a clean rainbow swirl on smooth bubbles, the model is mostly teal with patches of other colours on a dimpled surface; median hue difference 49 degrees, 39% of pixels within 30 degrees. At 256 cells 12 degrees and 69%, the swirl is there but mottled. Sea urchins: the picture's balls are plain green, the model is speckled in every colour: 84 degrees at 128, 67 at 256, and still 51 degrees at offset 0 where the shape is right, so the colour fault is separate from the fins of t9-mesh-1. Arches and hoops: right in the large, speckled in the middle: 12 degrees (65% within 30) at 128, 5.5 (81%) at 256. For comparison the first check's trap solid (same Julia set, sphere shell of radius 1): 7.5 degrees at 128, 2.9 at 512, though its middle bubble is mottled too.
evidence: out/t9/mesh/pics/cmp-exbubbles-128.png ; same folder: sheet-cmp-ex.png, cmp-exurchins-128.png, sheet-offset0.png, cmp-trapsolid-128.png ; numbers in out/t9/mesh/check-edge.txt and check-d.txt
suggested_fix: Not isolated between the samples and the mesh. Likely src/js/30-shaders.js, the raw branch that sampleSlice() in src/js/40-render.js draws: for a trap that is the solid, a sample's colour is still worked out at the grid point, where another layer of the trap (another orbit step) is the nearest one, so neighbouring samples carry unrelated colours; move the point onto the trap solid's own surface before colouring it, as was done for ordinary solids in fix pass 7. Then check src/js/46-mesh.js meshPoint(): on a wall thinner than two cells the two ends of a grid edge can lie on different layers, and blending them gives a colour neither has; take the end nearer the surface there.

title: The warning "parts thinner than one cell ... can look unlike it" appears for a trap solid whose model matches the picture, and only from 192 cells on
repro: Open dist/v8.html, Julia mode, choose Basilica in #juliaPreset, Frame it, set 'In the 3D view the trap' (#col-solid) to 'Is the solid'. Save a 3D model at 128, then Discard and again at 192 and 256, reading #meshWarn each time. From the workspace root: PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 python out/t9/mesh/drive.py x trapsolid:128,96,192,256 trapsolid:512 then python out/t9/mesh/check.py trapsolid-128 trapsolid-192 trapsolid-256 trapsolid-512.
expected: No warning when the model follows the picture; the same answer for the same solid at neighbouring resolutions.

They came out as 216 loose pieces, so the model is rougher than the picture and can look unlike it. A higher resolution follows the picture more closely.' Count only pieces that reach outside the box of the largest piece (meshExtent() already measures how far all pieces reach), or require as well that the kept piece holds a small share of the surface or is clearly shorter than all pieces together, as the second sentence's test does.

title: With surface offset 0 on a hollow trap solid, "Keep only the largest piece" keeps an inside-out inner wall, and the readme prints a negative volume
repro: Open dist/v8.html, choose "Chain of bubbles" in the list Examples (#trapExamples), wait for the picture. In Save a 3D model type 0 into Surface offset (#meshOffset), press Enter, Start the model at 128 cells, save and read readme.txt. From the workspace root: PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 python out/t9/mesh/drive.py x exbubbles0:128 then python out/t9/mesh/check.py exbubbles0-128 ; picture out/t9/mesh/pics/cmp-exbubbles0-128.png.
expected: The chain of bubbles, or at least a piece of its outside; never a surface that faces inward; a positive volume.
actual: The model is one ball: the inner wall of the middle bubble (it reaches 0.56 lab units from the centre), with its faces turned inward. Panel: Size '100 x 90.5 x 100 mm', Pieces 'The largest of 124, with about 40% of the surface'. Readme: 'Volume: -447.2 cubic centimetres' and 'The surface is closed: it has no holes and no loose edges, so it can be printed.' Overlap with the picture 0.46, 54% of the picture's outline missing. A slicer or Blender would take it for a solid ball turned inside out. At the starting offset 0.5 the same example gives the chain (overlap 0.946).
evidence: out/t9/mesh/checks/exbubbles0-128.json (readme, stl.volume_cm3 -447.19, components_with_negative_volume 1, lab_bbox_min, lab_bbox_max) ; same folder: pics/sheet-offset0.png (first row), check-d.txt, log-d.txt
suggested_fix: src/js/46-mesh.js, meshPieces(): the largest piece is chosen by its number of triangles. Work out each piece's signed volume and choose among the pieces whose volume is positive (a piece with negative volume is the wall of a cavity and belongs to the piece around it). In meshReadme() never print a negative volume or the sentence 'so it can be printed' for such a result.

title: A pinch that reaches a zoom limit stops without a word, while the wheel and the buttons say why
repro: Needs real touch: PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 python out/t9/camera/real.py phone, then read the lines 'pinch in at the nearest limit' and the one after it in the output. By hand on a touch screen at 375 x 812: type 0.5 in the box at the left end of the zoom row, tap the left end of the row, then spread two fingers on the picture: the distance stays 0.5 and no note about the limit appears. Now tap the + button: the note 'This is the nearest the zoom may go. The box at the left end of the slider sets that limit.' appears. The same at the far end (pinch together at 60).
expected: The same short note that the wheel, the plus and minus keys and the two buttons give when the zoom rests on a limit, since on a phone the pinch is the main way to zoom.
actual: The pinch is held at the limit silently. In the run the picture still showed the older note from a refused box value after the pinch (so the pinch wrote none), and the tap on + that followed replaced it with the limit note. In the frozen source, camPinch() in base8/js/50-camera.js sets cam.dist = clampDist(cam.dist * f) and never calls camNote(); camZoomTo() does.
evidence: out/t9/camera/real-phone.log: 'pinch in at the nearest limit: distance, note :: [0.5, "The farthest limit must be at least twice the nearest limit..."]', then 'the note at the limit names the box at the left end of the slider'. Picture real-phone-limit-note.png in the same folder. Seen once; not repeated on a state with no older note on show.
suggested_fix: src/js/50-camera.js, camPinch(): when the clamp changes the asked value and the view already rests on that limit (3D distance and 2D span), call camNote() with CAM_TEXT[camKind()].stop[0 or 1], with the same 'left end / right end' wording camZoomTo() uses while the slider is a row.

title: At the low end of Trap thickness, Surface threshold and Fly speed the arrows leave the step grid and never come back to round values
repro: On dist/v8.html, Colour and light: set 'In the 3D view the trap' to 'Is the solid' so that Trap thickness shows (starts at 0.05, toggle ±0.005). Click its down arrow ten times, then its up arrow three times, reading the box each time. The same on 'Surface threshold, pixels' in Quality and speed (type 0.1 first) and 'Fly speed, units per second' in View (type 0.02 first). expected: The arrows move in steps the user can follow: either the lowest value the arrows reach is on the step grid, or the first press up from the lowest value lands on the next grid value (0.005 for Trap thickness), so that 0.01 and 0.05 can be reached again with the arrows.
actual: Trap thickness: 0.05, 0.045 ... 0.01, 0.005, then 0.0005 (ten times thinner in one press), and up from there 0.0055, 0.0105, 0.0155 and so on to 0.0505. Surface threshold: 0.1, 0.05, 0.02, then up 0.07, 0.12, 0.17. Fly speed: 0.02, 0.01, 0.001, then up 0.011, 0.021, 0.031. The round values are only to be had again by typing or with the slider. title: "Ray step, share of the distance estimate" at 1.5 or more leaves the whole picture blank, and nothing says why
repro: Run: PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 python out/t9/walk/once4.py (prints the share of the picture that is not background for five values in four scenes). By hand on dist/v8.html: wait for the opening picture, open Quality and speed, click in the typed box of "Ray step, share of the distance estimate", select all, type 1.5, press Enter. The box accepts it without Extreme ranges (typed values up to 2 are taken). Or tick Extreme ranges and drag that slider to the right: the walk got 1.88 that way (out/t9/walk/run13/actions.jsonl, steps 30 to 32). Same result after "Twin of the Mandelbulb", "Twin of the Lathe" and in Julia mode. Not tried on dist/v6.html, so I cannot say whether it is new in Version 8.
expected: What the dial's help promises: "Higher is faster and can punch holes." So a solid with holes or missing thin parts, getting worse as the value rises; or a range that stops before the picture is lost; or a sentence on the picture saying the ray step is too large.
actual: At 1.2 (the right end of the ordinary slider) the picture is still there (9.0% of the stage not background against 11.8% at 0.8). At 1.5, 1.88 and 2 the stage is completely empty in all four scenes (0.007% to 0.015%, which is only the edges of the overlays), the status line reads "Done: 12 passes at 862 x 701", no note appears, and Reset view does not help. The user has to guess that this dial did it.
evidence: out/t9/walk/once4.log (all twenty readings), sheet-raystep.png in the same folder (opening picture and Julia set at 1.2 beside the empty stage at 1.5), once3.log lines "B.", and from the walk run13/b0032-seen.png and run13/f0032-BLANK.png (seen in sheet-blank.png).
suggested_fix: Either src/js/30-shaders.js, the march loop (the line "float stride = (rough ? d : d + LEVEL * e) * uStepK;"): find why a share of 1.5 loses every ray at once instead of some of them (for instance cap the share actually used, as 40-render.js already does for the Kleinian view with Math.min(S.q.stepk, 0.5)); or src/js/80-ui.js, the dial qd('qstepk', ...): its typed limit (hi: 2) and its Extreme range (xmax: 2, xhi: 4) reach values at which there is no picture, so end them where the picture still shows. I did not locate the exact value between 1.2 and 1.5 where the picture goes.
